source: user-supplied HackerOne Informative and Not Applicable adjudications
purpose: negative controls for program-impact and capability-delta triage

cases.technical_behavior: OIDC value appears in Runtime Logs when DEBUG is enabled
cases.starting_authority: runtime-log reader
cases.missing_security_proof: independent project-identity boundary and concrete protected use of the short-lived token
cases.unblock: prove the role cannot obtain equivalent identity and the token reaches a protected action unavailable to that role

cases.technical_behavior: provider-controlled skill path changes install scope and broadens installed provider content
cases.starting_authority: provider already selected to supply agent skills
cases.missing_security_proof: independently trusted victim artifact or new protected capability
cases.unblock: prove overwrite and automatic use of a distinct trusted skill with concrete protected impact

cases.technical_behavior: repository-local Windows command shim executes and receives a project token
cases.starting_authority: attacker-controlled repository trusted for local tooling execution
cases.missing_security_proof: pre-trust or higher-privilege capability beyond repository code execution
cases.unblock: prove execution or token exposure before trust or across a stronger sandbox/privilege boundary

cases.technical_behavior: signature key identity and code-signing EKU identity differ
cases.starting_authority: serverAuth-scoped signing credential
cases.missing_security_proof: current program-eligible high-impact downstream artifact acceptance
cases.unblock: prove a real protected consumer and impact meeting the current program severity floor

cases.technical_behavior: repository configuration changes deployment root and collects an out-of-tree file
cases.starting_authority: repository contributor plus destination project reader
cases.missing_security_proof: documented source-root boundary and recipient without equivalent project access
cases.unblock: prove upload to a principal or project not otherwise readable or controllable by the attacker

cases.technical_behavior: linking evaluates executable repository configuration
cases.starting_authority: trusted repository with documented programmatic config
cases.missing_security_proof: explicit non-execution promise or pre-trust execution
cases.unblock: prove the command crosses a documented inert/pre-trust boundary

cases.technical_behavior: callee omitted from one representation is directly accepted by another execution set
cases.starting_authority: model can invoke the same callee through a documented caller
cases.missing_security_proof: bypass of a supported approval or authorization control
cases.unblock: prove the direct route grants an action or arguments unavailable through all intended routes

cases.technical_behavior: signed precompute code can be replayed across compatible flag groups
cases.starting_authority: holder of a valid public rollout code
cases.missing_security_proof: SDK-owned authorization boundary and concrete protected effect without application misuse
cases.unblock: prove a program-owned protected action relies on the primitive as its documented security boundary

cases.technical_behavior: organization writer replaces an organization job artifact later run with creator-supplied secrets
cases.starting_authority: organization WRITE member trusted to create and modify org resources
cases.missing_security_proof: promised per-member isolation for the shared job artifact or secret consumer
cases.unblock: prove explicit denial of mutation/use for this member and a protected member-private consumer

cases.technical_behavior: read-scoped client creates a user-owned scheduled export that survives client deletion
cases.starting_authority: same user has view access to the exported analytics
cases.missing_security_proof: data beyond read scope or documented client-revocation cascade to user resources
cases.unblock: prove cross-principal data disclosure or an explicit revocation invariant

cases.technical_behavior: cloud deployment archive dereferences a tracked symlink into ignored local bytes
cases.starting_authority: source contributor influencing a deployment checkout
cases.missing_security_proof: program-recognized tracked-source isolation and unauthorized protected recipient
cases.unblock: prove the tool promises source-root isolation and attacker receives protected bytes without equivalent authority

cases.technical_behavior: trusted project environment redirects a credential-bearing client connection
cases.starting_authority: repository configuration accepted through directory trust
cases.missing_security_proof: pre-trust execution, narrower consent, or bypass of the workspace trust control
cases.unblock: prove the credential leaves before trust or outside the configuration authority explicitly granted

cases.technical_behavior: an unrelated website reaches an unauthenticated loopback development WebSocket, mutates extension assets, and obtains execution plus authenticated read capability inside the active development preview
cases.starting_authority: external website visited by a developer running an active local preview
cases.missing_security_proof: program-eligible effect outside the development-preview impact ceiling, such as protected production merchant data, non-development authenticated action, credential replay, or persistence
cases.unblock: prove a current in-scope production effect beyond the local preview context that meets the program's written impact bar

cases.technical_behavior: a public web origin reads synthetic mailbox data from an unauthenticated local demo API with permissive CORS
cases.starting_authority: website visited by the single operator of a documented local-only demonstration application
cases.missing_security_proof: a production product or supported multi-user deployment whose authentication or origin boundary the program defends
cases.unblock: prove the same root cause on a current eligible production asset with a cross-user protected-data boundary and no duplicate prior art

cases.technical_behavior: the local user's Git URL rewrite changes the destination after a managed marketplace URL check
cases.starting_authority: the same local user can deliberately modify the Git configuration used by the enforcing client
cases.missing_security_proof: an administrator-versus-user enforcement promise that remains authoritative despite user control of the downstream resolver configuration
cases.unblock: prove a distinct lower-privilege actor can alter resolution without controlling the policy subject's local environment or that the feature explicitly promises resistance to such user changes

cases.technical_behavior: automatic skill setup follows an attacker-planted workdir symlink and replaces a same-named directory outside the workdir
cases.starting_authority: party already trusted to populate the self-hosted worker's working directory in a model that provides unrestricted shell access
cases.missing_security_proof: a protected host boundary not already available through the accepted workdir and execution authority
cases.unblock: prove the symlink is introduced by a lower-privilege principal and reaches a protected host resource unavailable through all intended worker capabilities

cases.technical_behavior: DNS rebinding reaches an unauthenticated quickstart API, reads demo transcripts, and approves a tool inside the operator's own hosted sandbox session
cases.starting_authority: website visited by the single operator of a documented unauthenticated local quickstart
cases.missing_security_proof: a production or multi-user product boundary, credential disclosure, or effect outside the quickstart-created session
cases.unblock: prove the same primitive against an eligible production asset or a protected cross-user resource the program states the local service must defend

cases.technical_behavior: explicit DEBUG mode records a credential-bearing request-body field while default logging does not
cases.starting_authority: operator who enables documented full request and response body logging and exposes those logs to another reader
cases.missing_security_proof: a documented guarantee that DEBUG output redacts body credentials or a default/non-consensual logging path
cases.unblock: prove credential disclosure at a supported default level or a violation of an explicit schema-aware redaction guarantee

cases.technical_behavior: a deleted API key remains authorized by a warmed positive cache and can perform a protected write until expiration
cases.starting_authority: holder of a previously valid key who primed the cache before revocation
cases.missing_security_proof: novelty or eligibility because the program knew the issue and remediation was already in progress before submission
cases.unblock: none for the same root cause; retain the technical validation separately but pursue only materially distinct, independently novel roots

cases.technical_behavior: an unrestricted same-UID shell reads credential-bearing parent-process metadata despite best-effort child environment scrubbing
cases.starting_authority: model-controlled unrestricted shell in the worker's UID and PID trust domain
cases.missing_security_proof: a documented process-isolation boundary or capability unavailable to the unrestricted same-UID execution context
cases.unblock: prove the product promises isolation from the parent process or that a constrained tool without equivalent same-UID access crosses the credential boundary

cases.technical_behavior: a raw lockfile source line causes a privileged evaluator to fetch a private Git source that becomes readable through the shared Nix store
cases.starting_authority: workspace author who can already declare an ordinary Git dependency for the same repository
cases.missing_security_proof: a fetch or disclosure capability not attainable through the documented dependency declaration path
cases.unblock: prove attacker input accepted as inert by the supported format triggers access to a protected repository that no equivalent valid dependency declaration can fetch

cases.technical_behavior: configuration hierarchy differences cause dependency metadata to be interpreted from a lower-trust registry already selected by workspace configuration
cases.starting_authority: operator-configured replacement registry controls metadata for artifacts still constrained by the lockfile
cases.missing_security_proof: introduction of an unauthorized artifact, identity, or capability outside the configured registry and locked artifact set
cases.unblock: prove the differential selects bytes or authority outside the victim's locked and configured trust set and reaches a protected consumer

cases.technical_behavior: opening an untrusted project can cause startup loading of a disabled PKCS#11 library from an attacker-selected UNC path
cases.starting_authority: attacker can convince a Windows user to open a supplied project while project trust remains disabled
cases.missing_security_proof: reliable exploitation on the program's accepted default or common Windows configuration without extra firewall, share, policy, credential, or mapping prerequisites
cases.unblock: reproduce on a program-accepted stock configuration, freeze every network prerequisite, and obtain program confirmation that the untrusted-project mode promises to block this startup load

cases.technical_behavior: a limited editor can move an unauthorized page across permission subtrees and gain edit and delete authority in a local reproduction
cases.starting_authority: authenticated limited editor against a repository whose last maintenance activity was many years earlier
cases.missing_security_proof: a live production system operated by the program and running the vulnerable component
cases.unblock: prove the exact vulnerable code is currently deployed on an eligible production asset and reproduce the cross-subtree authorization transition there safely

cases.technical_behavior: attacker-controlled HTML rendered by the user can receive a credential-bearing Site map response from another context
cases.starting_authority: user intentionally selects or leaves active a mode that executes and completes attacker-controlled HTML
cases.missing_security_proof: execution and credential-context substitution without consent to active rendering or despite a documented isolation guarantee for rendered responses
cases.unblock: prove automatic execution under the safe/default viewer or a documented guarantee that Render never reuses responses across credential contexts

cases.technical_behavior: tracker-proxy converts client-supplied forwarding headers into an authenticated visitor IP that can evade IP-based spam bans
cases.starting_authority: unauthenticated tracking client in a deployment whose edge or web-server topology determines whether forwarding headers are trustworthy
cases.missing_security_proof: a product-owned trusted-proxy invariant independent of operator front-end configuration and an impact the program recognizes beyond analytics pollution
cases.unblock: prove the current supported deployment promises direct-client header rejection or trusted-proxy enforcement and demonstrate a protected effect beyond the operator-selected visitor-IP model

cases.technical_behavior: top-level manifest validation remains valid while an embedded ingredient exposes its invalid state and exact failure through nested validation results
cases.starting_authority: application consuming a layered validation API with both summary and ingredient-level result surfaces
cases.missing_security_proof: a documented guarantee that the top-level state enforces strict ingredient-chain validity or a default protected consumer that accepts an artifact it must reject
cases.unblock: prove the API contract requires nested invalidity to fail the top-level state and trace the mismatch into a concrete unauthorized acceptance decision

cases.technical_behavior: an attacker-chosen protobuf source path injects Rust through a generated line comment and executes when generated code is compiled and run
cases.starting_authority: party trusted to supply schema and descriptor metadata to a build-time code-generation pipeline
cases.missing_security_proof: a build-input isolation promise or execution capability unavailable through other trusted schema, manifest, or build inputs
cases.unblock: prove a lower-trust schema-only source is contractually non-executable and cannot reach equivalent build-time execution through any intended input

cases.technical_behavior: a WordPress role downgrade is not immediately reflected in Matomo, so a still-valid Application Password continues using the previously synchronized Matomo authorization until synchronization
cases.starting_authority: former administrator retaining a valid authentication credential issued while legitimately privileged
cases.missing_security_proof: a documented invariant that every WordPress role mutation immediately revokes Matomo authorization or the existing credential itself
cases.unblock: prove the product promises immediate cross-system authorization revocation for that role-change path and that no supported credential or synchronization lifecycle permits the stale state

cases.technical_behavior: an already fully authenticated session reaches a 2FA enrollment path that returns recovery codes and replaces the TOTP secret without sibling password reauthentication
cases.starting_authority: attacker already controls a fully authenticated account session
cases.missing_security_proof: a program-recognized step-up boundary that intentionally withholds persistent credential-management capability from an authenticated session
cases.unblock: prove the program treats recent-password or existing-factor verification as an independent security boundary and demonstrate durable access unavailable to the starting session

cases.technical_behavior: an authenticated request that overlaps logout-all can write its stale session state back after deletion and temporarily restore the old cookie
cases.starting_authority: attacker already holds a valid session and must keep a request in flight across the exact revocation moment
cases.missing_security_proof: an attacker-controllable and reliably exploitable overlap window under realistic production request timing without a lab-only table lock
cases.unblock: measure a realistic unprivileged trigger, success rate, timing window, and persistence against all supported revocation actions including password change

cases.technical_behavior: a read-scoped OAuth client creates a scheduled export to an external address and the user-owned report survives deletion of the OAuth client
cases.starting_authority: principal already authorized to read the same analytics and create reports owned by its Matomo login
cases.missing_security_proof: data beyond existing view authority or a documented client-revocation cascade over separately user-owned scheduled reports
cases.unblock: prove cross-principal data access or an explicit lifecycle guarantee that deleting the OAuth client revokes reports created under that delegated lineage

cases.technical_behavior: a session created with the old password in the same one-second timestamp bucket as a password change can remain authenticated
cases.starting_authority: attacker knows the victim's valid password, already has full account access, and must win a sub-second race with the password change
cases.missing_security_proof: material added authority or realistic reliability sufficient for the current program's severity threshold
cases.unblock: prove a practical post-revocation capability materially beyond the starting full-account authority and impact meeting the written program bar

cases.technical_behavior: skill bootstrap follows a repository-controlled workdir symlink and deletes, writes, then cleans up a same-named directory outside the configured workdir
cases.starting_authority: repository contributor already trusted to populate a self-hosted worker workdir whose toolset includes unrestricted shell execution
cases.missing_security_proof: a protected host capability not already implied by the accepted workdir and worker-user execution authority
cases.unblock: prove a distinct lower-trust source can plant the symlink and modify a protected resource unavailable through every intended worker capability

cases.technical_behavior: a legacy release-management endpoint lets a user without release-delete remove another operator's scheduled release insert while the newer endpoint rejects the action
cases.starting_authority: authenticated release operator with create and modify but without delete permission
cases.missing_security_proof: concrete release-integrity consequence severe enough for the program after the engineering team assessed the validated effect as minimal
cases.unblock: prove a current production release disruption or protected integrity consequence that meets the program's written severity and impact requirements

cases.technical_behavior: a signed shareable URL code reveals raw unlisted request-derived flag values and reconstructs the same state when replayed without the original request context
cases.starting_authority: party able to observe or receive a precompute URL intentionally designed to reconstruct flag state
cases.missing_security_proof: a documented confidentiality or encryption boundary for the signed code and a first-party protected secret placed there by an intended product flow
cases.unblock: prove the current contract promises confidentiality rather than integrity and demonstrate disclosure of program-owned sensitive data that the supported precompute flow itself places in the URL

cases.technical_behavior: a mirror configuration key containing URI userinfo is copied into Bundler's User-Agent and sent to an unrelated project gem source, where the credential can be replayed
cases.starting_authority: attacker controls a gem source referenced by the project while the operator has a global mirror key containing authenticated URI userinfo
cases.missing_security_proof: authoritative evidence that credential-bearing mirror source keys are a supported realistic configuration rather than credentials being stored only as protected values
cases.unblock: establish current official support or native tests for authenticated mirror-key userinfo, reproduce on the current release, and prove access to a protected unrelated registry with no equivalent attacker authority

cases.technical_behavior: an attacker-controlled configured gem source supplies a crafted name tuple that writes a constrained gemspec path outside the intended cache before SafeMarshal validation
cases.starting_authority: malicious or compromised gem source selected as a package trust anchor by the user
cases.missing_security_proof: a protected local capability not already available to a hostile trusted source through ordinary package metadata, package contents, or installation behavior
cases.unblock: prove the source is lower trust than ordinary package content and that the path write reaches a protected target unavailable through all intended source-controlled inputs

cases.technical_behavior: a disabled or trashed form ID continues creating subscribers, list membership, and welcome-email tasks through the anonymous subscription endpoint
cases.starting_authority: unauthenticated party that previously observed public form metadata
cases.missing_security_proof: a material confidentiality, availability, account, or cross-site impact above subscriber and mailing-list integrity
cases.unblock: prove an impact class and magnitude the current program rewards, such as protected-content disclosure, account compromise, cross-site effect, or meaningful availability loss

cases.technical_behavior: an authenticated uploader can finalize a shared partial upload and receive victim prefix bytes when temporary state is not bound to user or session
cases.starting_authority: authenticated uploader who must match another user's exact filename and extension while an uncommon incomplete upload remains present
cases.missing_security_proof: a reliable way to learn or predict the collision key and encounter a victim partial upload at meaningful frequency
cases.unblock: measure real filename entropy, partial-upload prevalence and lifetime, collision success rate, and an attacker-controlled discovery channel for the exact name and extension

cases.technical_behavior: malformed JSON Any values are accepted and canonicalized to empty or default wire messages before handler logic
cases.starting_authority: client able to invoke the handler and submit a well-formed empty or default Any producing the same application-visible state
cases.missing_security_proof: a handler state or protected operation reachable only through the lenient differential rather than an equivalent valid request
cases.unblock: identify a current production consumer where the malformed representation bypasses a security check that rejects every semantically equivalent well-formed input

cases.technical_behavior: an SSL-incapable runtime intentionally falls back to HTTP update metadata that an on-path attacker can modify and render in an administrator page
cases.starting_authority: on-path attacker against an operator-selected legacy runtime without SSL-capable transports
cases.missing_security_proof: a current security guarantee forbidding the documented fallback and realistic prevalence on supported production deployments
cases.unblock: prove the current program treats authenticated update transport as mandatory on that supported runtime and demonstrate material admin action on a realistic deployed configuration

cases.technical_behavior: a peer with incoming data access disabled can still participate in connectivity checks, exchange endpoint candidates, and trigger traversal probes
cases.starting_authority: authenticated Meshnet peer permitted to participate in the connectivity control plane but denied final incoming data traffic
cases.missing_security_proof: bypass of the enforced data-plane permission or documentation that the incoming permission also forbids connectivity-check control messages
cases.unblock: prove final protected incoming traffic or another denied capability succeeds, or establish an explicit product invariant gating the traversal control plane with the same permission

cases.technical_behavior: the official RPM installer uses nogpgcheck and accepts an unsigned substituted package whose post-install script executes as root
cases.starting_authority: attacker controls the TLS path serving both package content and publisher key material in the stated interception model
cases.missing_security_proof: a counterfactual in which enabling package signature verification prevents the same attacker from substituting a signing key or otherwise installing equivalent content
cases.unblock: prove package-body substitution without authority to alter the pinned trust root, then show enforced signature verification blocks that attacker on the exact supported path

cases.technical_behavior: a transfer package signed and attested before denylisting remains permissionlessly redeemable afterward while fresh deposits and new attestations are blocked
cases.starting_authority: the same depositor already signed the destination-specific transfer, already received Circle's attestation, and can use an intended withdrawal path for the same balance
cases.missing_security_proof: a protocol promise that denylisting retroactively revokes already-issued attestations or a distinct victim whose funds or authority are affected
cases.unblock: prove a post-denylist operator signature, theft or movement outside the depositor's preauthorized bounds, or an explicit retroactive-revocation invariant compatible with settlement correctness

cases.technical_behavior: a revoked FxA bearer remains accepted until its cached introspection result expires and can retrieve a Relay-native API token that remains usable after the FxA bearer expires
cases.starting_authority: an actor who possessed a valid FxA bearer and could retrieve the same Relay API token during the bearer's original authorized lifetime
cases.missing_security_proof: a documented lineage rule requiring FxA revocation or expiry to invalidate the separately issued Relay token, plus proof that the stale cache creates authority unavailable before revocation
cases.unblock: establish the official derived-token revocation contract and show an attacker obtains or retains a protected capability that was not already mintable or readable while the original bearer was valid

cases.technical_behavior: a payer-signed cancel authorization omits attester identity, so another registered attester can consume the nonce and force the payer to re-sign a payment intent
cases.starting_authority: a configurator-approved attester holding a cancel signature whose signed fields intentionally authorize nonce consumption and a bounded fee to the payer-selected beneficiary
cases.missing_security_proof: a realistic channel exposing another flow's cancel signature and a protected outcome beyond the payer's signed authorization or recoverable per-nonce denial
cases.unblock: prove the protocol promises attester-bound cancellation, demonstrate unauthorized value movement, or show reliable material denial beyond one retryable nonce using a signature the attacker can realistically obtain

cases.technical_behavior: after a local user edits a saved federation profile target, the first request reuses a fresh cached token for the previous workspace or service account
cases.starting_authority: the same local user or process controls both the profile configuration and adjacent credentials file containing the cached token
cases.missing_security_proof: an attacker-victim split or protected target inaccessible to the local principal that already owns the cached credential
cases.unblock: prove a lower-trust actor can cause the target switch without reading or using the credential cache and thereby obtain access outside the identity or organization already authorized

cases.technical_behavior: a trusted PR review run created for head A later reads workflow and job-log content from force-pushed head B through a live head lookup
cases.starting_authority: the same PR author already controls CI and log content for both heads, while the workflow token has repository-wide actions-read permission and only write-authorized users can trigger the action
cases.missing_security_proof: a later snapshot controlled by a stronger or different principal, or a trigger-time snapshot guarantee that serves as an enforced security boundary rather than a relevance filter
cases.unblock: show later-head content comes from an otherwise unauthorized principal or reaches a protected action that equivalent trigger-head untrusted content cannot influence

cases.technical_behavior: a reused libcurl handle can send a Digest response derived from one peer's challenge and the user's password to another peer when parsed challenge state lacks an origin binding
cases.starting_authority: a malicious second server can receive an authentication-derived Digest header for public challenge parameters under a specialized handle-reuse and auth-mask transition
cases.missing_security_proof: successful acceptance by the protected first peer, replay or oracle capability beyond public challenge data, and a realistic application path using the required reuse sequence
cases.unblock: demonstrate end-to-end authentication to the original protected peer with the captured or freshly induced response on a current real consumer, including nonce, method, URI, and replay-control behavior

cases.technical_behavior: an ETag response truncates stdout redirected by the user with append mode when --etag-save selects stdout, replacing prior contents of the chosen file
cases.starting_authority: the user explicitly directs a single-ETag output stream into a local file while the remote peer controls whether an ETag exists and its value
cases.missing_security_proof: a protected file or security decision for which this immediately observable explicit-output bug creates material confidentiality, integrity, or availability impact
cases.unblock: identify a supported production workflow where an untrusted peer reliably destroys security-critical state outside the intended semantics and prove the resulting protected consequence

cases.technical_behavior: curl_mprintf reads a double for documented long-double conversions, producing garbage and an uninitialized-value diagnostic on some ABIs
cases.starting_authority: a downstream application developer explicitly chooses the discouraged printf API, format, and long-double argument
cases.missing_security_proof: remote reachability, a shipped production consumer, and attacker-observable disclosure of protected bytes rather than incorrect numeric output or control flow influenced by undefined data
cases.unblock: find a current production consumer with attacker-reachable formatting whose returned output reproducibly contains protected process data across a real trust boundary

cases.technical_behavior: the HTTP/3 UDP path reconnects an application-provided socket despite CURL_SOCKOPT_ALREADY_CONNECTED and sends QUIC datagrams to the URL destination
cases.starting_authority: an application deliberately supplies a preconnected UDP descriptor through specialized callbacks and selects HTTP/3
cases.missing_security_proof: a current production application that treats the callback-selected peer as an enforced egress or relay boundary and suffers a protected consequence
cases.unblock: demonstrate the behavior in a shipped consumer whose documented security policy depends on the already-connected socket and prove unauthorized network reach or data exposure

cases.technical_behavior: --libcurl emits example C code that reuses one easy handle, causing --insecure from an earlier operation to persist across --next even though the CLI itself resets local options
cases.starting_authority: a developer explicitly requests generated example source, reviews or compiles the incomplete output, and deploys it without restoring per-operation security options
cases.missing_security_proof: a product guarantee that generated code is a security-equivalent executable and a current production consumer that deploys the affected output into an attacker-reachable TLS path
cases.unblock: prove an officially supported generated-code workflow consumed unchanged by a shipped application and demonstrate a real network attacker crossing its intended TLS verification boundary

cases.technical_behavior: an anonymous embed cache omits Referer from its key and can serve another origin's postMessage target, preventing iframe resize until the cache entry expires
cases.starting_authority: an unauthenticated requester able to prime the same public embed cache variant before a victim loads it
cases.missing_security_proof: resolution of the apparent conflict with the program's current cache-poisoning severity examples, realistic victim prevalence and cache-hit reliability, and the exact prior-knowledge timeline
cases.unblock: preserve dated live-at-submission evidence, verify current policy wording and prior knowledge, and measure a repeatable material availability effect on an eligible live deployment

cases.technical_behavior: a documented strict sandbox can fail to apply in a no-TTY session while a repository-defined MCP child still starts and writes outside the documented roots
cases.starting_authority: an attacker controls repository configuration processed by a user who explicitly selected the strict sandbox
cases.missing_security_proof: the requested realistic attacker-victim reproduction and timely response to the program's Needs More Info request; the closure did not adjudicate the technical merits
cases.unblock: complete the concise end-to-end victim workflow and all requested evidence before the response deadline, then obtain a merits-based program decision

cases.technical_behavior: a local WordPress and Nginx harness serves image derivatives after the primary attachment path is denied by an imported VIP ACL component
cases.starting_authority: an anonymous requester knows a previously public derivative URL
cases.missing_security_proof: reproduction through the complete WordPress VIP production file-handling stack rather than a partial locally assembled environment
cases.unblock: demonstrate the same disclosure on an authorized VIP environment or an exact production-equivalent stack including every middleware and file-serving layer

cases.technical_behavior: a user-approved custom RPC follows a 307 redirect to loopback, preserves JSON-RPC POST data, and returns a compatible local service response to the dApp
cases.starting_authority: a malicious dApp convinces the user to add and switch to its attacker-controlled custom RPC endpoint
cases.missing_security_proof: an explicit promise that approval is restricted to one origin and excludes redirects, plus a concrete protected local service and capability unavailable through the trusted RPC relationship
cases.unblock: prove a documented per-hop destination boundary and demonstrate compromise of a realistic protected service outside the authority delegated to the approved RPC

cases.technical_behavior: an opt-in browser background fetch follows a public redirect to loopback and causes a blind unauthenticated GET without returning the response
cases.starting_authority: a public page operator can cause the victim to visit its URL while the optional background feature is enabled
cases.missing_security_proof: a same-URL top-level navigation redirect control proving the background component adds network capability, and a concrete protected local service affected by the blind request
cases.unblock: compare ordinary top-level navigation and background fetch against the exact redirect under identical browser settings, then prove a protected local action only the latter can reach

cases.technical_behavior: a locally cached transaction validly signed before key revocation retains isVerified and is accepted by one test node after a later permission update
cases.starting_authority: the old key validly signed and submitted the transaction while still authorized, and the harness controls requeue ordering while stubbing consensus checks
cases.missing_security_proof: unmodified multi-node canonical acceptance and finality despite independent nodes revalidating the transaction against the updated permission state
cases.unblock: prove attacker-controlled inclusion and canonical finality on a production-equivalent multi-node network without consensus stubs or privileged scheduling

cases.technical_behavior: a trusted on-path actor can rewrite an unsigned HTTP status while preserving signed headers and body, causing the client to log out and clear local session state
cases.starting_authority: a trusted on-path interceptor can alter response framing but not the application-signed body
cases.missing_security_proof: an eligible terminal impact other than denial of service under a program that explicitly excludes DoS
cases.unblock: demonstrate an in-scope confidentiality, integrity, authentication, or authorization consequence that is not merely forced logout or service disruption

cases.technical_behavior: a release verification helper executes build inputs from the supplied tarball and can report that the tarball reproducibly rebuilds itself
cases.starting_authority: the verifier chooses an untrusted tarball while the documented authenticity anchor is the release signature and the helper warns against blind trust
cases.missing_security_proof: an explicit current guarantee that the helper independently authenticates provenance without a trusted signature or source tree
cases.unblock: show a signature-valid malicious release that passes while violating a precise documented verifier security property that users are instructed to rely on

cases.technical_behavior: anonymous invoice pages expose counterparties, amounts, descriptions, history, messages, and document filenames while direct file downloads remain private
cases.starting_authority: an anonymous visitor accesses invoice pages intentionally designed for transparency and unauthenticated viewing
cases.missing_security_proof: a product promise that page metadata or filenames are private rather than only the uploaded document bytes, plus eligibility under a program paused except for critical issues
cases.unblock: prove anonymous access to the private document contents or another field explicitly covered by a current confidentiality guarantee and meeting the program's active severity floor

cases.technical_behavior: Cardano VerifyMessage accepts a valid signature and claimed address without binding Blake2b-224 of the public key to the address payment credential
cases.starting_authority: an attacker owns an unrelated Cardano signing key and can construct a fresh signed challenge naming a victim address
cases.missing_security_proof: bounty novelty because the same missing public-key-to-address validation had already been submitted and was tracked under an earlier report
cases.unblock: retain the technical invariant but submit only a target-specific variant with a distinct root cause, protected consumer, or impact not covered by the earlier report; a private duplicate unknowable before submission is not a preventable research failure

cases.technical_behavior: a recursively fetched Git submodule gemspec executes in a Dependabot Bundler update and can request configured private-registry content through the job credential proxy
cases.starting_authority: repository-controlled dependency code is intentionally processed inside an update job designed to execute untrusted package code and resolve the configured registry
cases.missing_security_proof: an eligible boundary beyond updater-job execution and intended dependency resolution, such as sandbox escape, unauthorized private-network reach, raw secret extraction, or cross-tenant data access
cases.unblock: prove a currently eligible impact explicitly outside the updater sandbox and configured registry authority under the current Dependabot bounty policy

cases.technical_behavior: a plain HeaderRecord token field reaches the local-token path and returns an attacker-chosen Passport identity marked verified false and tokenSource local
cases.starting_authority: an unauthenticated HTTP caller can supply headers to an application that chooses an undocumented raw-header integration and decides whether the returned object is authoritative
cases.missing_security_proof: a real deployed integration or SDK contract that authenticates on a non-null identity despite the explicit unverified status
cases.unblock: identify a current shipped consumer using the affected input form and prove it grants a protected action while following documented SDK guidance or despite checking the verification status

cases.technical_behavior: an explicit link-local IPv6 proxy zone is parsed but not applied, so a multi-interface fallback can send plaintext proxy authentication to the same address on another interface
cases.starting_authority: an attacker controls the matching link-local endpoint on another interface while the user deliberately configures an unauthenticated transport to a literal link-local proxy
cases.missing_security_proof: a program-recognized confidentiality or route-isolation guarantee for the unsecured proxy mode and a realistic deployed topology where the remote attacker can establish all prerequisites
cases.unblock: demonstrate the same credential or traffic disclosure across an authenticated or encrypted proxy boundary, or prove an explicit route-isolation promise and a current production consumer

cases.technical_behavior: after CONNECT_ONLY a caller detaches a shared pool and raw I/O resolves a pool-local connection ID to an unrelated connection
cases.starting_authority: the application itself creates both pools and connections, enables CONNECT_ONLY, detaches the share after transfer, and then invokes raw I/O
cases.missing_security_proof: a remotely triggerable current production consumer whose attacker can force the complete unusual API lifecycle and cross a protected peer boundary
cases.unblock: prove the full sequence in a shipped application where an untrusted peer controls the transition and receives protected bytes without application misuse

cases.technical_behavior: repairing simultaneously closed stdin and stderr with opposite pipe ends can feed verbose proxy-authentication diagnostics into a stdin-based HTTPS upload
cases.starting_authority: a local launcher closes descriptors zero and two while deliberately requesting verbose mode, proxy authentication, and an upload sourced from the closed stdin descriptor
cases.missing_security_proof: remote attacker control of the launch configuration, portable descriptor behavior, and a current shipped workflow that unknowingly satisfies all prerequisites
cases.unblock: demonstrate a real deployed wrapper whose remote peer can reliably trigger the credential transfer without controlling local process launch or command-line construction

cases.technical_behavior: a GCC plus Apple SecTrust build can discard a nonempty stapled OCSP response while treating certificate verification as successful
cases.starting_authority: a network attacker has a hostname-valid but revoked certificate and targets a client compiled with a niche GCC, CMake, OpenSSL, and Apple SecTrust combination
cases.missing_security_proof: evidence that any current production or shipped consumer uses the affected compiler and TLS-backend configuration
cases.unblock: identify and reproduce against a current distributed application or supported binary using the exact affected configuration and prove invalid OCSP acceptance end to end

cases.technical_behavior: after project MCP approval is cleared and a changed authorization-server metadata URL is approved again, the client sends a previously stored refresh token to the newly configured server
cases.starting_authority: an attacker can modify MCP configuration inside a workspace the user chose to trust, and the user explicitly approves the changed project server configuration
cases.missing_security_proof: a credential-recipient isolation promise that survives approval of changed trusted-workspace configuration and a resulting capability unavailable through equivalent trusted-workspace hooks, MCP definitions, settings, or execution paths
cases.unblock: prove token disclosure before trust or without renewed approval, or prove an explicit authorization-server binding guarantee whose bypass grants authority unavailable through every other capability of the trusted workspace

cases.technical_behavior: a transitive crate's normalized links metadata can replace direct-dependency metadata and cause attacker-controlled source to be embedded in builder output
cases.starting_authority: the attacker-controlled crate is already present in the victim's locked dependency graph and can execute its own build script during the same build
cases.missing_security_proof: a protected build or data capability beyond the crate's existing build-time code execution, or a documented lower-trust metadata-only boundary that forbids equivalent build-script effects
cases.unblock: prove the influencing dependency cannot execute code or otherwise modify the build under the supported configuration, then demonstrate that the metadata collision alone crosses a protected direct-dependency or secret boundary
